entry.name: H-Tac DeskTask-Tac
entry.title: Human-Centric Transferable Tactile Pre-Training for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary: Bimanual desktop tasks by people wearing a 137-channel pressure glove on each hand, recorded at 30 Hz with MANO hand pose, wrist and head-camera pose and head-mounted RealSense D435 video; finger pose comes from multi-view keypoint triangulation (RawHand) or MANUS Quantum mocap gloves plus AprilTags (AprilTag).
entry.hand: Human hands, both gloved: 137-channel tactile glove ('TacGlove') on each hand; MANUS Quantum mocap gloves over them in the AprilTag pipeline

sensor.note: tactile.left_tacglove and tactile.right_tacglove: float32 (137,) per frame, integer values 0-180 in the 14 sample episodes (units not stated), resampled to the 30 fps first-person camera timeline. tactile_pred.* is the same vector one frame later (tactile_pred[t] == tactile[t+1] in all 14 episodes). The channel-to-sensor map is not released; UniTacHand (same authors) splits the 137 channels into thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky, palm and 'bend' regions. The paper projects the glove onto 891 MANO UV vertices and a 351-taxel UniTacHand space for training; the release carries the raw 137-D vectors.
sensor.maker: custom (Peking University / BeingBeyond; vendor not named)
sensor.model: TacGlove (name used in the release field names)

scale.text: Paper: 37.2 h, 947 episodes, ~4M frames at 30 Hz (the DeskTask-Tac part of the 160 h H-Tac). Released: 14-episode sample (10 RawHand, 4 AprilTag), 22,078 frames (~12.3 min), 12 task names

entry.access: Hugging Face BeingBeyond/H-Tac_Sample, ungated: 14 DeskTask-Tac episodes (LeRobot v2.1-style parquet + one head-camera MP4 each); the GitHub README says the full H-Tac release is 'coming soon' (checked 2026-10-16).
caveats: Only the DeskTask-Tac part of H-Tac (37.2 h of 160 h) is catalogued. HOI-Tac (~106 h, 124.8K sequences) derives binary contact from hand-object mesh distance in 14 public datasets (ARCTIC, DexYCB, OakInk, ...), and InternData-Tac (17.8 h, 9,563 episodes) projects simulated robot-gripper contact patches (Genie1, Lift2, Split ALOHA) onto a MANO hand; neither is measured touch on a hand, so both are excluded.
Released data is a 14-episode, ~12.3 min sample of the 947 announced episodes; the same repo also holds 84 InternData-Tac episodes (351-D simulated tactile), which are not human touch.
The Hugging Face card has no license tag; the MIT terms are in the LICENSE file of the sample package ('Copyright (c) 2026 H-Tac dataset authors'). The code repository is Apache-2.0.

Tactile values are raw integer counts (0-180 in the sample) with no stated unit; many channels read above zero at rest, and 0-73 of the 137 channels per hand stay at zero for a whole episode. AprilTagPip episode_000001 (operate_calculator): 73 right-glove channels read zero throughout and the right hand shows no contact.
state.dexhand_position, action.dexhand_position and the MANO beta (shape) vectors are all zeros in the 14 sample episodes.
AprilTag episodes: wrist pose and MANO theta are exactly zero in frames where a hand was not tracked (6-177 frames per hand per episode).
Only one camera view is released (video.top_view, the head-mounted first-person RealSense view despite its name); the two external D435 views and depth are not in the sample.
The project URL printed in the paper (beingbeyond.github.io/TTP/) returned 404 on 2026-10-16; the page is at research.beingbeyond.com/ttp.

unconfirmed: Tactile glove maker and model: the TTP paper says only 'a tactile glove'; the release calls it TacGlove (field names). UniTacHand (arXiv 2512.21233, same first authors) uses 'a custom pressure-sensitive tactile glove providing 137-dimensional tactile readings' with 'pressure-sensitive fiber sensors'; the identical 137 dimensions suggest the same glove, which neither source states.
Sensor principle: TTP section 4.2 says 'We project piezoresistive tactilities from different embodiments onto these taxels'; the glove itself is not described as piezoresistive in so many words.

Coverage tip/phalanx/palm: from UniTacHand's region list (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky, palm, bend) and the glove photo in TTP Fig. 3 (sensor strips along the fingers); the per-channel layout is not released. Some of the 137 channels may be bend channels rather than pressure taxels ('bend' region in UniTacHand).

MoCap glove = MANUS Quantum Metagloves: the paper says 'motion capture (MoCap) glove'; 'QUANTUM' is printed on the glove module in Fig. 3 and the release has manus_frame_index / manus_frozen_left / manus_frozen_right fields.
frames = 4,000,000 is the paper's '~4M'; 37.2 h x 30 Hz x 3,600 = 4.02M.
Sample size: 10,974 + 11,104 = 22,078 frames (meta/dataset_info.json) / 30 fps = 736 s (~12.3 min); durations from meta/episodes.parquet 20.2-202.9 s.

Tasks: DeskTask-Tac's task count is not stated (H-Tac in total: 300+). The sample has 12 distinct task names (10 RawHand, 3 AprilTag, play_tangram in both). Subjects, objects and scene count not stated.
Native glove sampling rate not stated; all streams are resampled to the first-person camera timeline (timestamp step 33 ms median; 4-6 duplicate timestamps in two AprilTag episodes).

video.top_view is the head-mounted first-person camera: the view shifts with head motion between frames 1 s and 22 s of RawHandPip episode_000009 and the hands enter from the bottom edge; the card calls it 'top-view'. The probed file is H.264 High 1280x720, 30 fps, 723 frames = 723 parquet rows.
Camera model 'Realsense D435' is the label in the project-page figure; the paper text says 'Three RealSense cameras'.
Wrist position unit: not stated; ranges 0.07-0.57 suggest metres.
Recording dates from timestamp_ms (unix ms) in the sample: AprilTag episodes 2026-01-28 to 2026-02-04, RawHand episodes 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-05.
RawHandPip episode_000000 right channel 7 holds half-integer values equal to half of channel 6 in 1,057 frames, which looks like interpolation of a dead channel (not documented).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~520 MB: 8 parquets (~18 MB; all 14 DeskTaskTac parquets, 32 MB, already in the survey scratch dir) + 8 top-view MP4s (15.5 + 24.9 + 40.5 + 49.1 + 29.3 + 48.7 + 30.8 + 263.7 MB = ~502 MB; AprilTag episode_000000 is cut to 66.5-121.6 s). Re-hosted media: re-encode to H.264 at a lower bitrate (source ~5 Mbps, 1280x720) to stay under ~30 MB per episode. Episode JSON: 2 x 137 integer channels at 30 Hz is ~0.45M values for the 55 s window, about 1.5 MB, so drop tactile_pred (duplicate of tactile shifted by one frame) and downsample hand pose if needed to stay under 2 MB.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 12 distinct task names in the release (more than 6), so 8 are taken, spanning both hand-pose pipelines (6 RawHand, 2 AprilTag/MANUS), different actions (fold, wipe, press/insert, pinch, operate an articulated lamp, grasp-place, manipulate a cylinder, arrange tangram pieces) and different objects. Not taken: play_doll, make_fruit_basket, organize_exam_pouch (69.9 s), and operate_calculator (AprilTagPip episode_000001: right glove 73 of 137 channels zero, no right-hand contact). One episode per task, 8 in total. All sampled episodes show contact on both hands for at least 1 s (glove sum more than 100 counts above the episode's 5th percentile) and have both 137-channel vectors in every frame with no NaN. Length: seven are 20-42 s; play_tangram (202.9 s) is cut to a 55 s window. Budget: within 2 MB JSON (see fetch_estimate), ~30 MB media per episode after re-encoding, 20 GB download.
deviations: The release does not label subjects or scenes, so episodes cannot be spread over subjects; they are spread over the two collection pipelines instead.

No glove channel map is released, so the grid layout of the 137 channels will have to be drawn as a plain 137-cell strip or derived from UniTacHand's region grouping (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky, palm, bend), which gives no per-channel indices.
